description:
The Krshak Prashikshan Tatha Bhraman Karyakram is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance the skills and knowledge of farmers across the country. 

This program was officially launched on 1st April 2018. 

It aims to provide farmers with practical training and exposure to modern agricultural practices. 

The initiative is part of the broader strategy to improve agricultural productivity and sustainability in India. 

The primary objective of the Krshak Prashikshan Tatha Bhraman Karyakram is to empower farmers with the latest knowledge in agricultural techniques. 

The program focuses on disseminating information about advanced farming methods, crop management, and sustainable practices. 

It also aims to increase farmers' income by improving their productivity and enabling them to adopt new technologies. 

The program targets a measurable increase in agricultural output by at least 20% over a five-year period. 

The initiative is designed to reach over 1 million farmers annually across various states in India. 

Farmers participating in the program receive comprehensive training sessions conducted by agricultural experts. 

These training sessions cover a wide range of topics including organic farming, pest management, and soil health. 

Farmers also gain insights into the use of modern equipment and technology in agriculture. 

The program includes field visits to successful farms and agricultural research centers. 

These visits allow farmers to observe best practices in action and learn from successful peers. 

The benefits of the Krshak Prashikshan Tatha Bhraman Karyakram extend beyond just knowledge. 

Farmers are also provided with financial assistance for adopting new technologies. 

The program allocates a budget of ₹100 crore annually for training and capacity-building activities. 

Each participating farmer can receive up to ₹10,000 as a subsidy for purchasing modern agricultural tools and equipment. 

Eligibility for the program is broad to ensure maximum participation. 

Farmers of all ages are eligible to apply. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to participate in the program. 

However, preference is given to small and marginal farmers who own less than 2 hectares of land. 

The application process for the Krshak Prashikshan Tatha Bhraman Karyakram is straightforward. 

Farmers must fill out an application form available at local agricultural offices or online through the official government portal. 

Required documents include proof of land ownership, identity proof, and a recent passport-sized photograph. 

Farmers are encouraged to submit their applications at least one month prior to the scheduled training sessions. 

The program is implemented through the Department of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

State agricultural universities and local agricultural departments play a crucial role in executing the training sessions. 

The program is designed to be flexible and adaptive to local agricultural conditions. 

Training sessions are conducted in regional languages to ensure better understanding among farmers. 

The frequency of the training sessions varies by state but is generally conducted quarterly. 

Farmers can expect to receive training updates and schedules through local agricultural offices. 

Disbursement of financial assistance occurs within two months of completing the training program. 

Farmers are required to submit proof of purchase for any equipment to receive the subsidy. 

The Krshak Prashikshan Tatha Bhraman Karyakram also emphasizes the importance of women in agriculture. 

Special sessions are organized to encourage female farmers to participate actively. 

The program aims to increase women's participation in agriculture by at least 30% over the next five years. 

Feedback from participants is collected to continuously improve the training modules. 

The program has reported a significant increase in the adoption of organic farming practices among participants. 

Approximately 40% of trained farmers have shifted to organic methods post-training. 

The initiative has also led to a notable increase in the use of bio-fertilizers and bio-pesticides. 

The program has been well-received in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Maharashtra. 

In these states, the program has successfully trained over 250,000 farmers in its first year alone. 

The Krshak Prashikshan Tatha Bhraman Karyakram is part of the larger vision of the Government of India to double farmers' income by 2022. 

The initiative aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

The program also promotes the use of digital technology in agriculture. 

Farmers are trained on using mobile applications for weather forecasts and market prices. 

The initiative has a dedicated helpline for farmers to seek assistance and guidance. 

This helpline operates from 9 AM to 6 PM on weekdays. 

The contact number for the helpline is 1800-180-1551. 

The Krshak Prashikshan Tatha Bhraman Karyakram is a vital step towards modernizing Indian agriculture. 

It aims to create a knowledgeable and skilled farming community. 

The program is expected to contribute significantly to food security in India. 

By enhancing farmers' skills, the initiative also aims to reduce rural poverty. 

The government continues to monitor the program's impact through regular assessments. 

Overall, the Krshak Prashikshan Tatha Bhraman Karyakram represents a comprehensive approach to agricultural development in India. 

It combines education, financial support, and practical experience to empower farmers. 

The initiative is a crucial part of India's efforts to achieve sustainable agricultural growth. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this program to improve their livelihoods. 

The government remains committed to supporting farmers through various initiatives like this one.
